text:
Anu: Quick sanity check — velvET-v2 embeddings after int8 quant show a recall@10 regression on the longtail test set. Posting the quick numbers we ran in staging.

Ben: ah ok — how big is the regression?

Anu: overall recall@10 unquant = 0.862, int8 per-layer = 0.789 (delta -0.073). recall@1 unquant = 0.612, int8 = 0.538. silhouette (kmeans) went from 0.34 -> 0.28.

Priya: that 7.3ppt drop at @10 is nontrivial. Is this concentrated on short queries / long queries?

Anu: it's skewed to longtail (query freq < 5). For top-10k frequent queries drop is ~0.01.

Kai: do we have cosine shift distributions? median cosine between quant and float for same docs?

Anu: median cosine(sim(float, int8)) = 0.976 for head, 0.942 for tail. tail has heavier left tail. I uploaded per-query deltas to the run: https://internal.rw/run/velvet-v2-int8-20260318 (public to eng team).

Ben: thanks. any obvious outlier dimensions? could be a small set of heads blowing up after symmetric quant.

Anu: we inspected per-dim variance. A few dims show large clamp-induced shifts — looks like activation range estimation used max without outlier clipping.

Priya: did you try per-channel quant or static range clipping?

Anu: quick ablation: per-channel int8 + 1% histogram clipping => recall@10 = 0.842 (delta vs float -0.02). recall@1 = 0.587. silhouette 0.31. So per-channel + clipping recovers most of the quality.

Kai: nice — that's a decent tradeoff. What's the latency/cost hit?

Anu: per-channel adds ~6% token latency on our inference path and model size same on disk but slightly worse memory layout for our kernel (we saw +8% vram working set). Cost estimate still ~40% lower than float32 due to memory bandwidth.

Ben: can we instead do hybrid quant — int8 for trunk, fp16 for a small set of top layers? maybe keeps perf and lowers QoS hit.

Anu: quick test: keep last 2 layers fp16 + int8 elsewhere => recall@10 = 0.855, recall@1 = 0.605, latency +3% vs baseline int8. Looks promising.

EvalBot: automated eval summary: dataset=semantic-longtail-v1, metric=recall@10, float=0.862, int8(per-layer)=0.789, int8(per-channel+clip)=0.842, hybrid(fp16-tail)=0.855, notes="per-channel quant + clipping best quality/cost tradeoff".

Priya: good. For rollout plan I'd prefer per-channel+1% clip as default quant profile and offer hybrid fp16-tail as a "compatibility" variant in model catalog. Add unit tests for longtail recall and a smoke that checks recall@10 delta <= 0.03 vs float.

Kai: agree. Also add a monitoring eval that computes median cosine shift and triggers if >0.03 for customer traffic.

Anu: will add:
```
# quick commands we ran
rw-eval run --model velvet-v2 --quant-profile per_channel_clip1p --dataset semantic-longtail-v1 --metrics recall@1,recall@10,silhouette --out /runs/velvet-v2-int8-20260318
```

Anu: I'll open a PR with the quant profiles, unit tests, and the experiment logs. Leaving notes on the run page with the per-query top diffs.

Ben: thanks — can you also dump a small set (100 queries) with worst delta for manual inspection? I'd like to check if labeling or querying mismatch is amplifying the effect.

Anu: on it, will post list here when ready. :thumbsup:

Priya: and add release notes to model-catalog: mention expected tail regression and recommended profile.

Anu: noted. I'll tag @Kai and @Ben on the PR.

Kai: :eyes: thanks everyone.
